title: Valuing Rail Access Using Transport Innovations (Gibbons & Machin)
publisher: LSE Centre for Economic Performance (DP 611); Journal of Urban Economics 2005
key_point: New Jubilee/DLR stations: +9.3pp price growth; 1.5-5.8% per km closer within 2 km; no effect beyond 2 km.

title: Valuing School Quality Using Boundary Discontinuities (Gibbons, Machin & Silva)
publisher: LSE SERC (DP 18); Journal of Urban Economics 2013
key_point: Boundary design: 1 SD school value-added or intake raises prices about 3%; parents pay for effectiveness and peers.

title: Game of Zones: The Economics of Conservation Areas (Ahlfeldt, Moeller, Waights, Wendland)
key_point: New conservation designations: no short-run effect, ~2.8% inside / 2.3% outside in one spec; gentrification drives designation.

title: Very Long-Run Discount Rates (Giglio, Maggiori & Stroebel)
key_point: England leaseholds vs freeholds: 80-99 yrs -16%, 100-125 yrs -10%, 125-150 -8%, 150-300 -3%.

title: The Time Value of Housing: Historical Evidence on Discount Rates (Bracke, Pinchbeck & Wyatt)
publisher: Economic Journal / Bank of England / LSE
key_point: Most London sales are long leases; implied discount rates decline with horizon; contradict practitioner relativity rules; houses +20% vs flats.

title: The Amenity Value of English Nature: A Hedonic Price Approach (Gibbons, Mourato & Resende)
publisher: LSE SERC (DP 74); Environmental and Resource Economics 2014
key_point: +1pp ward gardens/green/water share ~+1%; rivers -0.9%/km; National Park +5%; Green Belt £5,800 in metro areas.

title: The Costs of Urban Property Crime (Gibbons)
key_point: London: criminal damage cuts prices (1/10 SD = ~1%, £2,200); burglary has no measurable price effect.

title: The Impact of Supply Constraints on House Prices in England (Hilber & Vermeulen)
key_point: Regulatory constraints raised England prices ~35% by 2008; land scarcity binds in urban areas like London.

title: Gone with the Wind: Valuing the Visual Impacts of Wind Turbines through House Prices (Gibbons)
key_point: Visible wind farm within 2 km cuts prices 5-6%; hidden turbines no effect: views are capitalised.

title: Mind the Anticipation Gap: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis of the Elizabeth Line's Impact on London Housing Prices (Nguyen)
key_point: Elizabeth line: +4.9% within 1 km during construction, 7.7-8.1% at 2-10 km; -2.0% after 2022 opening.

title: The Economic Effects of Density: A Synthesis (Ahlfeldt & Pietrostefani)
key_point: 347 estimates; recommended density elasticity of rent 0.15; density a net amenity but regressive.

title: The Economics of Skyscrapers: A Synthesis (Ahlfeldt & Barr)
publisher: LSE CEP (DP 1704); Journal of Urban Economics 2022
key_point: Residential rent floor elasticity ~0.07 in NYC and Chicago, consistent with view/height amenity premium.

title: Does Energy Efficiency Matter to Home-Buyers? An Investigation of EPC Ratings and Transaction Prices in England (Fuerst, McAllister, Nanda, Wyatt)
key_point: Vs EPC D: A/B +5%, C +1.8%, E/F ~-1%, G ~-7%; larger for terraces and flats.

title: Is Flood Risk Capitalised into Property Values? (Beltran, Maddison & Elliott)
key_point: Meta-analysis 364 estimates: inland 100-yr floodplain -4.6% rule of thumb; -6.9% just after flood; coastal biased.

title: Assessing the Economic Benefits of Flood Defenses: A Repeat-Sales Approach (Beltran, Maddison & Elliott)
key_point: England 1995-2014: new flood defences raise urban prices 12.6-16.7%; rural prices fall 0.8-5%.

title: School Performance, Non-cognitive Skills and House Prices (Rossi)
key_point: Scotland catchment boundaries: ~3-4% per SD school attainment; no premium for value-added, unlike England.

title: The Impact of Airport Noise on House Prices (Kaur, Cardak & McAllister)
key_point: Melbourne: buyers ignore noise contours, price runway distance (up to 37%) and flight volume instead.

title: An investigation of the effect of EPC ratings on house prices
key_point: Vs EPC G: D +8%, C +10%, A/B +14%; effect insignificant in South East, smaller in London than North.

title: Energy efficiency ratings have limited impact on owner-occupied house prices, despite increased interest in 'going green'
key_point: Owner-occupier A/B vs D premium only 1.6%; F/G -1.4%; buy-to-let A/B premium 12.2%.

title: Value is in the eye of the buyer (In Focus: Prime Central London 2026)
key_point: PCL immaculate homes command ~30% premium over needing upgrade; values -26% from 2014 peak; houses outperform flats.

title: What makes prime central London different (lettings)
key_point: PCL rentals: immaculate condition 31% rent premium over moderate; 35% of tenants UK nationals.

title: How Does Emissions-Charging Influence House Prices? Evidence From London's ULEZ
key_point: Found via OpenAlex only; PDF inaccessible; London ULEZ house-price effect not verified.

title: Waiting on the train: The anticipatory (causal) effects of Crossrail in Ealing
key_point: Crossrail anticipation effects in Ealing; paywalled, title only seen via OpenAlex.
